audit.whatIsWrong: The single most useful mechanic in the matchup is absent: Decimate has a blade and a handle, and only the blade heals him.
audit.why: Riot's Decimate text: 'Enemies struck by the blade take more damage than those struck by the handle. Darius heals based on enemy champions and large monsters hit by the blade.' Standing inside the swing rather than at its edge turns a 9s heal-and-chunk into almost nothing. The page instead says to block it with Aegis Assault, which spends a 22s cooldown to solve a positioning problem.
audit.corrected: Stand inside Decimate at the handle — no heal, minimal damage — instead of spending Aegis Assault on it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four strings talk about his 'empowered Q' at five Hemorrhage stacks, and Apprehend is described only as a pull. Neither is right.
audit.why: Riot's Hemorrhage text: at max stacks 'Darius enrages and gains massive Attack Damage' — it empowers him, not one ability. Riot's Apprehend text has a passive half the page never mentions: it 'passively causing his physical damage to ignore a percentage of his target's Armor', which is why buying armour into Darius underperforms. Noxian Guillotine is true damage on top of that.
audit.corrected: Five stacks enrage him for massive AD; Apprehend passively shreds a percentage of your armour, and the ultimate is true damage — armour is the wrong purchase here.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown appears anywhere, which hides the biggest number in the matchup.
audit.why: Apprehend is 26 seconds at rank 1 — the longest cooldown either champion has, longer than Aegis Assault's 22s and twice Shield Vault's 13s. Baiting it buys you two full gap-closes. Decimate is 9s, Crippling Strike 5s, Noxian Guillotine 120s and it refreshes on a kill.
audit.corrected: Apprehend's 26s is now the sequencing anchor in the spikes, the cooldown block, the dos and the interactions row.

audit.why: The chart giving Darius four stages and Pantheon none reads harsh against 53.28% over 2198 games, but it is consistent with the prose: Pantheon's win rate comes from levels 1-2 and from Grand Starfall map play, not from any stage where Darius has Apprehend up. Levels 3 and 6 as Skill rows are the honest middle.

edits.before: Your level 1 and 2 are far stronger than his here — open with the point-and-click W stun and Q poke before Hemorrhage stacks or his empowered Q exist. Trade in short bursts and walk away; never sit in melee long enough for his bleed to tick or his outer-edge E to catch you. Bait his E pull, sidestep it, and punish the long cooldown with a W-in Q-tap reset.
edits.after: Your level 1 and 2 are far stronger than his — open with the Shield Vault leap-stun and Q poke before Hemorrhage can stack toward the enrage. Trade in short bursts and walk away. When you must be in melee, stand inside Decimate: the handle neither heals him nor hurts much, only the blade does. Bait Apprehend, sidestep it, and punish 26 seconds of nothing with a W-in Q-tap.

edits.before: Through 4-5 the lane tips to him: once his Hemorrhage is stacking and his passive-empowered Q is up, his sustained all-in beats your shield-and-burst frame. Use Aegis Assault (E) to block his empowered Q swing and the channel to refuse his apprehend trades, but stop committing to long duels. At 6 your Grand Starfall is for roaming, not 1v1ing Darius — use R to take over other lanes rather than coin-flip a melee against his execute.
edits.after: Through 4-5 the lane tips to him: with Hemorrhage stacking toward the enrage, his sustained all-in beats your shield-and-burst frame. Do not hold Aegis Assault for Apprehend — the pull drags you out of the channel. Answer Decimate by standing at the handle instead, and refuse long duels. At 6 Grand Starfall is for roaming, not 1v1ing a Guillotine that deals true damage and refreshes on a kill.

edits.before: Your point-and-click W stun and Q poke give you the strongest level-1 here before Hemorrhage or his empowered Q exist.
edits.after: Shield Vault's leap-stun and Comet Spear give you the strongest level 1 here, before Hemorrhage has a single stack on you.

edits.after: With all three basics it's even — handle-side Decimate denies his heal, but Hemorrhage's bleed still answers your burst.

notes: Two things worth the user's attention. First, ITEMISATION: Apprehend passively makes Darius's physical damage ignore a percentage of your armour and Noxian Guillotine is true damage, so the standard Plated Steelcaps answer is much weaker here than the page implies — the Itemization row still reads as a generic armour build and I could not restate it inside the length band. Second, I wrote that Apprehend's pull drags you out of an Aegis Assault channel; that rests on Riot's description of a forced pull plus the kit's own flag that the channel is 'interruptible — any CC cancels it', not on tested behaviour, so it is logged in unverified. Grievous Wounds is worth a line too: Decimate heals off every champion hit by the blade.
